scope: A selected corpus of appearance-related reports from seven major Sunni collections. Not exhaustive across all traditions, manuscripts, historical biographies, or transmission routes.
digestDefinition: SHA-256 of UTF-8 JSON.stringify of unique [primarySourceUrl, arabicFull] pairs, sorted by primarySourceUrl.localeCompare(otherUrl, 'en'). This fingerprints the audited transcription, not its scholarly authenticity.
method: All cited primary and related URLs were retrieved individually and their Arabic, narrator, numbering and displayed grading inspected.
English and Urdu are original summaries composed from the cited Arabic, not copied modern translations.
arabicFull preserves the complete primary-page arabic_hadith_full block, including isnad and any compiler or transmitter remarks inside that block.
Arabic extraction removed markup, decoded HTML entities, removed U+200E/U+200F formatting marks and collapsed whitespace. It did not reconstruct or emend the matn.
Every short Arabic excerpt occurs in its full report after Unicode NFC normalization. Entries sharing a primary URL preserve identical full Arabic.
Bukhari and Muslim use their conventional sahih collection classification. Other primary grades retain named displayed assessments. Related references do not inherit a primary grade.
Reference-check dates record source-page inspection, not independent scholarly authentication.
materialCorrections: Bukhari 3552 gives a moon comparison without explicit full-moon wording or facial measurements. Muslim 2344b explicitly supplies roundness and abundant beard hair.
Bukhari 3551 says red hullah; striped pattern and Yemeni manufacture were not asserted from this matn.
Muslim 2339 preserves Simak's explanation in response to Shu'ba. A long eye opening does not establish wide-set eyes.
Muslim 2332's displayed English text includes a cold-weather revelation sentence absent from its Arabic matn; it was not included in the summary.
Bukhari 5877 does include the ring inscription. Uncited correspondence context was removed.
Muslim 1359a is Amr ibn Huraith's sermon and black-turban account, not a dated conquest report. Muslim 1358a is Jabir ibn Abdullah's separate entry-into-Mecca account.
Bukhari 3561's initial excerpt came from related Muslim 2330a; it was replaced with the actual primary wording.
Shama'il 44's Arabic says oil concealed grey hairs; its displayed English reversal was not followed.
Shama'il 8 identifies Hind as al-Hasan's maternal uncle, not aunt. Its weak grading remains visible.
Differing named assessments at Tirmidhi 2811, Shama'il 17 and Shama'il 226 were preserved without inventing a different-chain explanation.
Aisha's laughter report concerns visibility of the back of the mouth, not loudness.
Abu Juhaifa's brightness account describes shins, not feet. The app's combined legs-and-feet theme does not change that anatomical wording.
Unsupported consensus, independent-chain, exact-measurement, garment-pattern and chronology assertions were removed from both languages.
remainingLimits: Entry counts are reading units, not independent chains or distinct historical observations.
Selected weak reports are included for research, prominently cautioned and excluded from the default established-reports view.
The famous long Umm Ma'bad description is not included: the inspected source did not provide that full appearance speech within the verified source set.
Knee and arm evidence in the supplement concerns observed posture, not unreported shape or dimensions.
This is research-assisted editorial work, not a critical edition, scholarly certification, or fatwa service.
